request: how does simple interest grow a £1000 loan?

beats.intent: Bars of the amount owed each year with 5% simple interest: 1000, 1050, 1100, 1150, 1200
beats.narration: Borrow a thousand pounds at five percent simple interest: you add fifty pounds every year.
beats.code:
stage.title("Simple interest")
bars = draw_bars(stage, [1000, 1050, 1100, 1150, 1200], labels=["year 0", "1", "2", "3", "4"])

beats.intent: Fresh axes with the straight line A = 1000 + 50t
beats.narration: Plotted against time it is a straight line: the same fifty every year.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 10), y_range=(900, 1600), labels=("years", "£"))
line = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda t: 1000 + 50 * t, color=YELLOW, label="1000 + 50t")

beats.intent: The point at 10 years, £1500, marked
beats.narration: After ten years you owe fifteen hundred pounds.
beats.code:
m = mark_point(stage, ax, 10, 1500, color=RED, label="£1500")
stage.equation(r"A = 1000(1 + 0.05t)")

request: what does it mean to be in the 90th percentile?

beats.intent: 100 dots in a row of scores sorted from lowest to highest
beats.narration: Line up a hundred test scores from lowest to highest.
beats.code:
stage.title("Percentiles")
dots = draw_dots(stage, n=100, cols=20, color=GREY_B)

beats.intent: The first 90 dots coloured blue and one red dot just after them
beats.narration: If ninety people scored below you, you are in the ninetieth percentile.
beats.code:
stage.play(*[dots[k].animate.set_color(BLUE) for k in range(90)])
stage.play(dots[90].animate.set_color(RED).scale(1.6))

beats.intent: The row beside 90% below you
beats.narration: It does not mean you scored ninety percent: it means ninety percent of people scored lower.
beats.code:
stage.caption("90% scored lower than you")
stage.equation(r"\frac{90}{100} \text{ below}")

beats.intent: A bar split into quarters with 3 shaded
beats.narration: Three quarters of a bar.
beats.code:
stage.title("3/4 or 5/8?")
q = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.7, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.7 if k < 3 else 0.1) for k in range(4)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0).shift(UP)
stage.play(Create(q))
stage.add(q)
stage.label(q, "3/4", direction=LEFT, color=BLUE)

beats.intent: A bar of the same length split into eighths with 5 shaded
beats.narration: Five eighths of an equal bar.
beats.code:
e = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=0.75, height=0.7, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.7 if k < 5 else 0.1) for k in range(8)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0).shift(DOWN * 0.3)
stage.play(Create(e))
stage.add(e)
stage.label(e, "5/8", direction=LEFT, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: A dashed line at the end of the 3/4 shading showing it reaches further, beside 3/4 = 6/8 > 5/8
beats.narration: Three quarters is six eighths, one eighth more than five eighths.
beats.code:
mark = DashedLine(q[2].get_right() + UP * 0.6, q[2].get_right() + DOWN * 2, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(mark))
stage.add(mark)
stage.equation(r"\tfrac34 = \tfrac68 > \tfrac58")

request: can rectangles with the same area have different perimeters?

beats.intent: Four rectangles each of area 24: 1×24, 2×12, 3×8, 4×6
beats.narration: Four rectangles, all with area twenty four: one by twenty four, two by twelve, three by eight, four by six.
beats.code:
stage.title("Same area, different perimeter")
s = 0.22
rects = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=w * s, height=h * s, color=c, fill_opacity=0.5) for (w, h), c in zip(((24, 1), (12, 2), (8, 3), (6, 4)), (RED, ORANGE, YELLOW, GREEN))]).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=LEFT)
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r) for r in rects], lag_ratio=0.3))
stage.add(rects)

beats.intent: Bars of their perimeters: 50, 28, 22, 20
beats.narration: Their perimeters are fifty, twenty eight, twenty two and twenty.

beats.intent: The shortest bar, the nearly square 4×6, lit
beats.narration: The closer to a square, the shorter the fence needed.
beats.code:
highlight(stage, bars[3], color=GREEN)
stage.caption("Closest to a square: least perimeter")

request: why does a circle hold the most area for its perimeter?

beats.intent: A triangle, a square and a circle, each with perimeter 12
beats.narration: Three shapes with the same perimeter, twelve: a triangle, a square and a circle.
beats.code:
stage.title("Most area for the fence")
tri = RegularPolygon(3, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5).scale(1.15).shift(LEFT * 4)
sq = Square(side_length=1.5 * 1.0, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.5)
circ = Circle(radius=12 / TAU * 0.5, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5).shift(RIGHT * 4)
stage.play(FadeIn(tri), FadeIn(sq), FadeIn(circ))
stage.add(tri, sq, circ)

beats.intent: Bars of their areas: triangle 6.9, square 9, circle 11.5
beats.narration: Their areas: about six point nine, nine, and eleven point five.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
bars = draw_bars(stage, [6.93, 9.0, 11.46], labels=["triangle", "square", "circle"])
highlight(stage, bars[2], color=GREEN)

beats.intent: The bars beside A = P²/(4π) ≈ 11.5 for the circle
beats.narration: For a given perimeter the circle always wins: that is why bubbles are round.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"A_{\text{circle}} = \frac{P^2}{4\pi} = \frac{144}{4\pi} \approx 11.5")

request: how much paint do I need for a wall with a window?

beats.intent: A wall rectangle 5 m by 3 m
beats.narration: A wall five metres wide and three metres high.
beats.code:
stage.title("Painting a wall")
wall = Rectangle(width=5, height=3, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.5)
stage.play(Create(wall))
stage.add(wall)
stage.label(wall, "5 m", direction=DOWN)
stage.label(wall, "3 m", direction=LEFT)

beats.intent: A 2 m by 1.5 m window cut out of it
beats.narration: It has a window two metres by one and a half, which does not need paint.
beats.code:
win = Rectangle(width=2, height=1.5, color=WHITE, fill_color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1).shift(RIGHT * 0.8 + UP * 0.2)
stage.play(FadeIn(win))
stage.add(win)
stage.label(win, "2 × 1.5", direction=UP, color=WHITE)

beats.intent: The wall beside 15 - 3 = 12 m²
beats.narration: The wall is fifteen square metres, the window three: twelve square metres to paint.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"5 \times 3 - 2 \times 1.5 = 12\ \text{m}^2")

request: why is 1 square metre equal to 10,000 square centimetres?

beats.intent: A square labelled 1 m by 1 m
beats.narration: A square one metre on each side.
beats.code:
stage.title("Square metres and centimetres")
sq = Square(side_length=4, color=BLUE)
stage.play(Create(sq))
stage.add(sq)
stage.label(sq, "1 m", direction=DOWN)
stage.label(sq, "1 m", direction=LEFT)

beats.intent: The square ruled into a 100 by 100 grid of centimetre squares
beats.narration: Each side is a hundred centimetres, so the square holds a hundred rows of a hundred small squares.
beats.code:
grid = VGroup(*[Line(sq.get_corner(DL) + RIGHT * 0.04 * k, sq.get_corner(UL) + RIGHT * 0.04 * k, stroke_width=0.4, color=GREY) for k in range(1, 100)],
              *[Line(sq.get_corner(DL) + UP * 0.04 * k, sq.get_corner(DR) + UP * 0.04 * k, stroke_width=0.4, color=GREY) for k in range(1, 100)])
stage.play(Create(grid), run_time=2)
stage.add(grid)

beats.intent: One tiny square lit beside 100 × 100 = 10,000 cm²
beats.narration: A hundred times a hundred: ten thousand square centimetres.
beats.code:
tiny = Square(side_length=0.04, color=RED, fill_opacity=1).move_to(sq.get_corner(DL) + np.array([0.02, 0.02, 0]))
stage.play(FadeIn(tiny))
stage.add(tiny)
stage.equation(r"100 \times 100 = 10\,000\ \text{cm}^2")
